$$\begin{array}{c|cc} & b_1 & b_2\\ \hline a_1 & (v_{11},-v_{11}) & (v_{12},-v_{12})\\ a_2 & (v_{21},-v_{21}) & (v_{22},-v_{22})\end{array}$$
A mixed strategy of player one is described by $q_1=p_1(a_1)$ (so $p_1(a_2)=1-q_1$) and of player two by $q_2=p_2(b_1)$ (so $p_2(b_2)=1-q_2$). Let $V(q_1,q_2)$ denote the expected payoff of player one.

Let $q_1^*,q_2^*$ be such that $V(q_1^*,q_2^*)=\max_{q_1}\min_{q_2}V(q_1,q_2)=\min_{q_2}\max_{q_1}V(q_1,q_2)$. Show that $(q_1^*,q_2^*)$ is a Nash equilibrium of the two-player two-action zero-sum game. (Player two's payoff is $-V$.)
smt-2023-power-2-14.answer: No profitable deviation for player one, because $q_2^*$ minimizes the maximum; none for player two, because $q_1^*$ maximizes the minimum.

smt-2023-power-3-01.prompt:
*Second price auction.* There are agents $1,\dots,n$ and one good; agent $i$ values the good at $v_i$ (all $v_i$ distinct) and bids $b_i$, all simultaneously. The agent with the highest bid wins the item and pays the second highest bid; the others pay nothing. If agent $i$ obtains the object at price $p$, their utility is $v_i-p$; otherwise it is $0$.

Write agent $i$'s utility as a function of $v_i,b_1,b_2,\dots,b_n$. In other words, define $u_i(b_1,\dots,b_n)$.
smt-2023-power-3-01.answer: $u_i=v_i-\max_{j\ne i}b_j$ if $b_i$ is the highest bid, and $0$ otherwise.
